raw_response:
I am thinking like this: my land is not much, only 10.9 mu, and there are just two of us at home, so I cannot spread myself too thin. Wheat and maize are still my steady crops, because I have done them many years and I know how they behave on my land. The vegetable plots bring cash, but they also need more watching, more spraying, more hand work, so I only keep them on smaller pieces I can manage well. I have a well, so I will use water when the crop is at the important stage, but I will not pour money into too many irrigations unless the weather is really dry.

For wheat, I will do about the same as the years that were decent: sow in early October, put base fertilizer first, then one more topdressing when the wheat starts to stand up and grow fast. After wheat harvest in June, I will hurry and plant maize right away on the same land, because if I delay, I lose moisture and yield. For tomato, eggplant, and watermelon, I will keep moderate area, use improved seed or seedlings I can get locally, give enough fertilizer to keep the plants strong, and spray only when I really see disease, insects, or bad weeds. I do not chase the highest yield. I just want steady harvest and money in hand, without spending so much that the family gets tight on cash.
